member.name: M:class_162.method_415(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary:
Using the first argument t, interpolate using (x1,x2,y1,y2) such that:
When t is x1, the output is y1.
When t is x2, the output is y2.
You can think of this as a 'remapping' operation, taking a value t in the range [x1,x2] and transforming it into an equivalent value in the range [y1,y2] instead.
The returned value will be as far along the [y1,y2] range as t is along the [x1,x2] range, for example if t is exactly halfway between x1 and x2, the output will be halfway between y1 and y2.
If t is outside the range [x1,x2], it continues to work the same.
member.returns: Interpolation result

member.name: M:class_162.method_416(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)

When t is x1, the output is y1.
When t is x2, the output is y2.
You can think of this as a 'remapping' operation, taking a value t in the range [x1,x2] and transforming it into an equivalent value in the range [y1,y2] instead.
The returned value will be as far along the [y1,y2] range as t is along the [x1,x2] range, for example if t is exactly halfway between x1 and x2, the output will be halfway between y1 and y2.
If t is outside the range [x1,x2] its output is clamped, such that it cannot be lower than y1 or higher than y2.
member.returns: Interpolation result

member.name: M:class_140.method_323(Vector2,Vector2,Vector2)
member.summary:
Draws a close button, and returns whether the current window should close, which can be because the button itself was pressed, because ESC was pressed, or because the player clicked outside of the window.
This method takes the position and size of the window it should be attached to, not of the button itself.
The button is rendered on the bottom-left of the rect/bounds2 defined by the two vectors by default. You can change this using .
Clicking not just outside the defined rect, but near the edges of the rect is taken as indication you wish to leave the window, and thus this function will then return true. This is due to a margin OM itself applies.
If you wish to 'cancel out' this margin and make it so that only clicks that are fully outside of the rect defined by and , it could be done by doing:
Bounds2 b = Bounds2.WithSize(ORIGINAL_POS,ORIGINAL_SIZE).Expanded(70f, 66f, 80f, 59f);
var shouldClose = UIUtils.CloseButton(b.BottomLeft, b.Size, ORIGINAL_OFFSET - new Vector2(70,66));
Or you could simply copy the contents of this function, and take out the part which handles this margin, if you need something similar but without the margin. I'm just saying this function does a bit more than it seems at a glance.
member.param: Position of the 'window' to close button will be drawn on.
Size of the window the close button will be drawn on.
member.returns: Whether the current screen/UI element should be closed.
